items.stem: During an active outage affecting customers, what should the response team prioritise first?

options.text: Mitigating impact to restore service, even with a temporary fix, before pursuing full root cause
options.rationale: Correct: restoring service for users comes first; root-cause analysis follows in the postmortem.

options.text: Completing a full root-cause analysis before taking any action
options.rationale: Waiting for full root cause prolongs customer impact.

options.text: Assigning blame to the engineer who made the last change
options.rationale: Blame is counterproductive and not a response priority.

options.text: Closing the incident quietly without informing stakeholders
options.rationale: Stakeholders must be kept informed during an incident.

items.explanation: Correct: restoring service for users comes first; root-cause analysis follows in the postmortem.

items.stem: Which statements describe a blameless postmortem correctly? (Select TWO)

options.text: It focuses on systemic contributing factors rather than individual fault
options.rationale: Correct: blameless postmortems examine how the system allowed the failure, not who to punish.

options.text: It aims to create psychological safety so people report issues honestly
options.rationale: Correct: removing blame encourages honest disclosure and better learning.

options.text: Its main output is identifying who to discipline
options.rationale: Discipline is explicitly not the goal of a blameless postmortem.

options.text: It should omit the timeline to keep the document short
options.rationale: An accurate timeline is essential to learning from the incident.

items.explanation: Correct: blameless postmortems examine how the system allowed the failure, not who to punish.; Correct: removing blame encourages honest disclosure and better learning.

items.stem: What makes an action item from a postmortem effective?

options.text: It has a clear owner, a due date and addresses a contributing factor
options.rationale: Correct: effective action items are specific, owned, dated and tied to a real cause.

options.text: It is written as a general aspiration with no owner
options.rationale: Unowned, vague items rarely get done.

options.text: It assigns collective responsibility to the whole company
options.rationale: Diffuse responsibility means no one acts.

options.text: It is marked done as soon as the postmortem is published
options.rationale: Closing it before the work is done defeats its purpose.

items.explanation: Correct: effective action items are specific, owned, dated and tied to a real cause.
